p: crown of pride: Meaning, the proud kingdom of the Israelites, who were drunk with worldly prosperity.

valleys of them that are overcome: Because the Israelites for the most part dwelt in plentiful valleys, he means by this the valley of them who had abundance of worldly prosperity and were as it were crowned with garlands.
strong one: He seems to mean the Assyrians, by whom the ten tribes were carried away.
the early fruit before the summer: Which is not of long continuance, but is soon ripe and first eaten.
remnant of his people: Signifying that the faithful who do not put their trust in any worldly prosperity but made God their glory, will be preserved.
strength to them that turn the: He will give counsel to the governor and strength to the captain to drive the enemies in at their own gates.
they also have erred through wine: Meaning, the hypocrites who were among them, and were altogether corrupt in life and doctrine, which is here meant by drunkenness and vomiting.
Whom shall he teach knowledge: For there was no one that was able to understand any good doctrine: but were foolish and as unfit as young babes.
precept must be upon precept: They must have one thing often repeated.
lips and another tongue will he: Let one teach what he can, yet they will no more understand him, than if he spoke in a strange language.
he said: That is, the prophet, whom God would send.
This is the rest with which: This is the doctrine on which you ought to stay and rest.
cause the weary to rest: Show to them that are weary and have need of rest, what the true rest is.

LORD was to them precept upon: Because they will not receive the word of God, when it is offered, it comes of their own malice, if after their hearts are so hardened, that they care not for it, as before, Isa 6:9.
covenant with death: They thought they had shifts to avoid God's judgments, and that they could escape though all others perished.
falsehood have we hid ourselves: Though the prophets condemned their idols and vain fruit of falsehood and vanity, yet the wicked thought in themselves that they would trust in these things.
tried stone: That is, Christ, by whom all the building must be tried and upheld, Ps 118:22, Mt 21:42, Ac 4:11, Ro 9:33, 1Pe 2:6.
shall not make haste: He will be quiet, and seek no other remedies, but be content with Christ.
righteousness to the plummet: In the restitution of his Church, judgment and justice will reign.
hail shall sweep away the refuge: God's corrections and affliction.
the hiding place: Affliction will discover their vain confidence, which they kept secret to themselves.
vexation only to understand the report: Terror and destruction will make you learn that which exhortations and gentleness could not bring you to.
shorter than that a man can: Your affliction will be so sore, that you are not able to endure it.
Perazim: When David overcame the Philistines, 2Sa 5:20, 1Ch 14:11.
of Gibeon: Where Joshua discomfited five kings of the Amorites, Jos 10:12.

even the face of it: As the plowman has his appointed time, and various instruments for his labour, so has the Lord for his vengeance: for he punishes some at one time, and some at another, some after one sort, and some after another, so that his chosen seed is beaten and tried, but not broken as are the wicked.
